card.name: First word after a section heading
card.fires_on: The first word of body text that comes right after a run-in subsection heading in drug labels, with no line break or period between them. Typical first words are There, Weight, The, To and In.

modes.label: Heading then There/The
modes.description: A common opening word starts the paragraph right after a warning or dosage heading.
modes.example: Cardiovascular Events with Sumatriptan<< There>> have been rare reports of serious cardiac adverse

modes.label: Heading word repeated
modes.description: The first word of the paragraph repeats the topic named in the heading.
modes.example: 5.3 Fluid Retention<< Fluid>> retention and peripheral edema are known effects

modes.label: Start of a split word
modes.description: The paragraph opens with the first piece of a longer word such as Dis or Post.
modes.example: 5.3 Discontinuation of Prasugrel Tablets<< Dis>>continue thienopyridines, including

card.writes: Little clear effect; it mildly favors ellipsis or truncation marks and disfavors line-ending symbols.
card.plain: It fires on the first word of a paragraph that follows a heading in a drug label, when the heading runs straight into the text.
